keyAndScale.modalCharacter: Swampy Stax Records minor-blues funk blending a dark C# minor pentatonic riff with biting dominant 7th turnaround chords
keyAndScale.relativeMinor: C# minor is the relative minor of E major

mainProgression.progressionDescription: An 8-bar/12-bar hybrid Stax blues structure: the band locks into a relentless 4-bar C# minor pentatonic unison riff during the verse before climbing to G#7 (V7) and F#7 (IV7) for the hook ('If it wasn't for bad luck, I wouldn't have no luck at all').
mainProgression.description: An 8-bar/12-bar hybrid Stax blues structure: the band locks into a relentless 4-bar C# minor pentatonic unison riff during the verse before climbing to G#7 (V7) and F#7 (IV7) for the hook ('If it wasn't for bad luck, I wouldn't have no luck at all').

sectionProgressions.description: Iconic single-note minor pentatonic riff walking from G# up through B to C# with a B-to-G# pull-off

sectionProgressions.section: Chorus Turnaround ('If it wasn't for bad luck...')
sectionProgressions.description: Sustained dominant seventh chords on the V and IV degrees answered by stinging Albert King bends
Call-and-response blues soloing in 9th position (C# minor pentatonic Box 1) and 11th position
C# minor pentatonic Box 1 (9th fret) and lower-register riff phrasing

harmonicFunction: C#7 / C#7#9 (I7) - Gritty blues tonic anchored by the hypnotic single-note unison riff
G#7 (V7) - Dominant fifth chord that halts the riff to spotlight the central lyrical hook
F#7 (IV7) - Subdominant seventh chord stepping down a whole tone before dropping back into the main riff

techniques.name: Syncopated Minor Pentatonic Riffing & Call-and-Response Bending
techniques.description: Locking a tight, funky single-note minor pentatonic bassline riff with quarter-step blue-note curls on the minor third (E) and answering every vocal line with expressive upper-register bends

sequence: Play the pickup notes on the 4th fret low E string (G#) and 2nd fret A string (B) leading into the 4th fret A string root (C#) on beat 1
Walk up to the 2nd fret D string (E) and 4th fret D string (F#), curling the E note slightly sharp
Finish the two-bar riff with the descending pull-off on the A string (4th fret C# → 2nd fret B → 4th fret low E G#)
Between vocal phrases, jump to the 9th-fret C# minor pentatonic box for stinging bends on the G and B strings
tips: Give the 2nd-fret D string (E, the minor 3rd) a slight quarter-step microtonal tug toward E# so it growls like a true Stax Records horn section
Keep your fretting hand relaxed so the riff sits deep in the Booker T. & the M.G.'s pocket at 88 BPM
When Cream covered this song, Eric Clapton transposed it to G minor—mastering it in C# minor lets you play along with the original Albert King track

sections.name: Iconic Unison Blues Riff
sections.description: Booker T. Jones and Steve Cropper's immortal Stax unison riff played with Donald 'Duck' Dunn and Albert King.
notes: Anchor your index finger at the 2nd fret and ring finger at the 4th fret
Apply a subtle quarter-step curl on the 2.4 (E) note
Keep the eighth and sixteenth notes tight and funky

sections.name: Chorus Turnaround ('If It Wasn't for Bad Luck')
sections.description: The V7 to IV7 turnaround (G#7 to F#7) resolving back into the C#7 unison riff.
notes: Strike G#7 at the 4th fret and let it sustain while the vocals deliver the hook
Drop down two frets to F#7 at the 2nd fret
Snap right back into the main C#7 riff on beat 1

sections.name: Albert King 9th-Position Call-and-Response
sections.description: Signature Albert King stinging lead phrase in the 9th-fret C# minor pentatonic box.
notes: Bend the 11th fret G string and 12th fret B string with authority
Let the high C# root (9th fret high E string) ring crisp and bright
Finish on the 11th-fret D string root C# with wide vibrato

guitar.recommended: 1958 Gibson Flying V ('Lucy') or Gibson ES-335 / Fender Telecaster (Steve Cropper rhythm)
guitar.pickup: Bridge + Neck humbuckers together for biting, hollow-midrange Stax blues tone

amp.recommended: Acoustic 260 Solid-State Amp or Roland Jazz Chorus / Fender Twin Reverb

effects.distortion: Light overdrive (or higher-gain Marshall Plexi crunch if playing the Cream version)
effects.other: Plucked with bare thumb (Albert King style) or a firm pick near the bridge

beginner.title: The Unison Riff & Turnaround Chords
steps: Learn the single-note C# minor pentatonic main riff in 2nd/4th position
Practice the G#7 (4th fret) and F#7 (2nd fret) dominant 7th barre chords
Play through the full verse and chorus structure at 75 BPM → 88 BPM

intermediate.title: Microtonal Curls & 9th-Fret Lead Fills
steps: Add the quarter-step blue-note curl on the 2nd-fret D string (E) inside the main riff
Learn the 9th-position C# minor pentatonic Box 1 lead licks
Alternate between playing the two-bar riff and answering with a one-bar lead lick

advanced.title: Albert King String Bending & Cream Variation
steps: Execute multi-step Albert King bends in the 9th and 12th positions using bare-thumb attack
Transpose the entire riff and solo to G minor to jam along with Eric Clapton & Cream's version
Improvise a full solo chorus with vocal call-and-response phrasing

commonMistakes: Playing the main riff with stiff, robotic timing instead of laying back into the funky Stax pocket
Forgetting the pickup notes on beat 4 ('and-a') leading into beat 1 of the riff
Jumping out of time when switching from the 2nd-position riff up to the 9th-position lead box
practiceRoutine: 5 minutes: Main unison riff looped continuously at 88 BPM focusing on pocket and the E-note curl
5 minutes: Jumping from the 4th-fret riff to the 9th-fret C# minor pentatonic box for 2-beat fills
5 minutes: Full song jam with backing track
focusAreas: Tight sixteenth-note pull-off at the end of the riff
Microtonal quarter-step curl on the minor third
Expressive call-and-response timing between vocal lines
metronomeWork: Start at 72 BPM to lock in the syncopated second measure of the riff
Set metronome to 88 BPM and accent beats 2 and 4
Practice landing on the 4th-fret A string (C#) squarely on beat 1 after every lead fill
